maria: Heads up — after yesterday's runtime rollout (attn-tile v2 + int8 quant profile), we're seeing a ~18% drop in initial-context cache hit rate for the chat-v2 route. P95 latency for cold requests jumped ~120ms. :eyes:

jack: Which metric? console or traces? can you paste the query?

maria: console per-route: `sum(cache.hits{route:chat-v2}) / sum(cache.lookups{route:chat-v2})` — baseline was ~0.84, after rollout ~0.68. Also seeing more kv-key-mismatch WARNs in runtime logs.

maria: snippet from runtime logs:
```
2024-10-12 03:12:21.842 WARN kvcache: key_mismatch route=chat-v2 session=xyz hash_a=0x7f8c12ab hash_b=0x3d9f0012 reason=key_digest_diff
2024-10-12 03:12:21.843 INFO cache: warmup_miss route=chat-v2 prefix_len=64
```

infra-bot: deploy event: runtime-rollout/attn-tile-v2 at 2024-10-12T03:00Z by @deploy-bot; canary 5% -> 100% finished.

ryan: We also landed a batching heuristic tweak in the same window (dynamic-size threshold lowered). Could be correlated. Did you check request size distribution?

maria: Yes — median seq_len same, but freq of short prompts increased slightly. Hit rate drops concentrated on sessions with repeated short prefixes (assistant system + user intro).

sophia: Possible causes: (1) kernel change altered internal ordering/strides so the cache key serialization differs, (2) quant profile changes introduced tiny fp -> int rounding in pre-key projection, producing different digests, (3) batching changes exposing concurrency race on cache insert.

jack: Can you reproduce locally with a deterministic trace? if we can show key bytes differ pre/post kernel that's gold.

maria: Reproducer command I used (dockerized runtime):
```bash
# reproduce on canary image
curl -s -X POST $CANARY_URL/gen -d '{"prompt":"<seed> hello \n", "session_id":"repro-123"}' -H 'Content-Type: application/json'
# capture kv key hex from logs
```

maria: example hex diff from two runs (before vs after):
```
pre:  a3 4f 7c 12 9d 00 11 24 9f ...
post: a3 4f 7c 12 9d 00 10 24 9f ...  # one byte flipped at pos 7
```

anil: one byte flip smells like non-deterministic pack/align or a change in key-serialization (endianness/padding). Did any of the attn kernels change the `KVKey::serialize` path?

maria: I grepped: the codepath is the same, but the kernel opcode added a small prefetch pad and we replaced a memcpy with tensor.copy_strided in one hotpatch. That could adjust memory layout.

jack: Quick mitigation: re-enable compatibility mode that forces canonical key normalization (enable `runtime.flags.kv_key_sanitize=true`) — will add CPU cost but should recover hit-rate. Can someone flip it in prod for chat-v2?

sophia: Also propose a fallback: route short prefixes to legacy kernel variant via runtime routing policy (canary variant) until we fix serialization. Less perf impact than global sanitize.

ryan: I'll own the reproducer + micro-benchmark. Plan: run A/B with 1000 identical short sessions against canary kernel with and without `kv_key_sanitize`, collect raw key bytes and hit counts. ETA 3 hours.

maria: assign to @ryan, thanks. I'll open a perf incident and attach the logs + console graphs.

deploy-bot: created incident INC-2024-847 in #incidents, priority P2, linked to runtime-rollout/attn-tile-v2.

jack: if reproducer confirms serialization diffs, we should push a small runtime patch to ensure deterministic packing (no padding) and add unit tests to lock bytes.

maria: Agreed. For triage: (1) hotfix: `kv_key_sanitize=true` on chat-v2 (QA & rollout), (2) run A/B reproducer (ryan), (3) patch runtime packing and add test, (4) revert sanitize and re-roll kernel.

sophia: I'll draft the test harness for key-byte regression and add it to pre-merge gate.

maria: Thanks all. tagging @jack @sophia @ryan for follow-up. Will update incident with reproducer results. :thumbsup:
